title: R-linear category
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. An *$R$-linear category* is a category $\mathcal C$ in which every morphism set $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$ is given the structure of an $R$-module, such that for all objects $x,y,z$ the composition $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(y,z)\times\Hom_{\mathcal C}(x,y)\to\Hom_{\mathcal C}(x,z)$ is $R$-bilinear: $(g+g')\circ f=g\circ f+g'\circ f$, $g\circ(f+f')=g\circ f+g\circ f'$ and $(ag)\circ f=a(g\circ f)=g\circ(af)$ for $a\in R$. In particular the underlying abelian groups make $\mathcal C$ a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category]; composition induces an $R$-linear map $\Hom(y,z)\otimes_R\Hom(x,y)\to\Hom(x,z)$. ($R$-linear categories are not assumed additive.)
